content: # Appendix D. Core literature supporting the VOC anchor
The literature update was completed before disease-effect access. The following sources support the anchor logic; they do not become study outcomes.
1. Chen J, et al. Exhaled volatolomics profiling facilitates personalized screening for gastric cancer. Cancer Letters. 2024;590:216881. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.canlet.2024.216881
- GC breath panel, prior aldehyde-oxidation/single-cell interpretation, and direct novelty comparator.
- Used for class occurrence and field positioning, not a frozen heptanal direction.

2. Huang L, et al. Noninvasive Diagnosis of Gastric Cancer Based on Breath Analysis with a Tubular Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Sensor. ACS Sensors. 2022;7:1439-1450. https://doi.org/10.1021/acssensors.2c00146
- GC breath carbonyl study including pentanal, hexanal, octanal, and decanal.

3. Kumar S, et al. Mass Spectrometric Analysis of Exhaled Breath for the Identification of Volatile Organic Compound Biomarkers in Esophageal and Gastric Adenocarcinoma. Annals of Surgery. 2015;262:981-990. https://doi.org/10.1097/SLA.0000000000001101
- Oesophageal/gastric adenocarcinoma evidence containing the C4-C10 straight-chain aldehyde series.
- Mixed disease grouping limits gastric specificity.
4. Markar SR, et al. Assessment of a Noninvasive Exhaled Breath Test for the Diagnosis of Oesophagogastric Cancer. JAMA Oncology. 2018;4:970-976. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamaoncol.2018.0991
- Multicenter evaluation retaining butanal and decanal in an oesophagogastric model.
5. Amal H, et al. Detection of precancerous gastric lesions and gastric cancer through exhaled breath. Gut. 2016;65:400-407. https://doi.org/10.1136/gutjnl-2014-308536
- Large GC/precancer breath study demonstrating the broader and heterogeneous gastric VOC landscape.

6. Mochalski P, et al. Identification of Key Volatile Organic Compounds Released by Gastric Tissues as Potential Non-Invasive Biomarkers for Gastric Cancer. Diagnostics. 2023;13:335. https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics13030335
- Paired gastric-tissue headspace; cohort-specific higher hexanal and nonanal and substantial between-cohort heterogeneity.

7. Huang J, Kumar S, Hanna GB. Investigation of C3-C10 aldehydes in the exhaled breath of healthy subjects using SIFT-MS. Journal of Breath Research. 2014;8:037104. https://doi.org/10.1088/1752-7155/8/3/037104
- Technical quantification of the complete saturated aldehyde window; propanal most abundant and C4-C10 present at trace levels.
8. McCartney MM, et al. Breath carbonyl levels in a human population of seven hundred participants. Journal of Breath Research. 2020;14:046005. https://doi.org/10.1088/1752-7163/ab8865
- Quantified C4-C10 straight-chain aldehydes in 692 participants and documented pre-analytical confounders.

9. Muller-Wirtz LM, et al. Quantification of Volatile Aldehydes Deriving from In Vitro Lipid Peroxidation in the Breath of Ventilated Patients. Molecules. 2021;26:3089. https://doi.org/10.3390/molecules26113089
- Experimental PUFA oxidation yielded pentanal, hexanal, heptanal, and nonanal; also demonstrates material contamination risk.
10. Chin ST, et al. Cross-platform mass spectrometry annotation in breathomics of oesophageal-gastric cancer. Scientific Reports. 2018;8. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-22890-w
- Demonstrates annotation challenges and the chemically diverse carbonyl landscape across MS platforms.
11. Bovey F, et al. Breath acetone as a marker of energy balance: an exploratory study in healthy humans. Nutrition and Diabetes. 2018;8. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41387-018-0058-5
- Supports the decision not to use ketones as a single gastric host-tissue anchor because acetone responds strongly to fasting and macronutrient balance.
12. Petralia LS, et al. The oral microbiome and its effect on exhaled breath volatile analysis. Journal of Breath Research. 2025;19. https://doi.org/10.1088/1752-7163/adf505
- Directly shows sampling-route dependence for several alcohols and other VOCs and supports explicit oral-source caution.
13. Hernandez-Leyva AJ, et al. The gut microbiota shapes the human and murine breath volatilome. Cell Metabolism. 2026;38:779-793.e8. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2025.12.013
- Supports the decision not to assign breath acids or other microbial VOCs to a gastric host-tissue transcriptomic program.
14. Wang et al. A 15-layer multi-omics analysis of gastric cancer ecotypes provides therapeutic insights. Cell Reports Medicine. 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.xcrm.2026.102756.
- Direct novelty comparator and processing authority for the CPTAC/LinkedOmics protein layer.
- Documents TMT13 exclusion and reprocessing, the broad fifteen-layer CPTAC scope, and phospholipid elimination during metabolite extraction.

The broader audited corpus also included Xiang 2023, Jung 2021, Hong 2021, Duran-Acevedo 2018, Tong 2017, Chen 2016, Xu 2013, Kumar 2013, Slefarska-Wolak 2022, Leiherer 2020, Mochalski 2018, and Zhang 2014. These studies document the diversity, platform dependence, cell-line heterogeneity, and frequent direction inconsistency of non-aldehyde candidates. They justify narrowing the formal question rather than expanding it.
